quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Mixed Reported Speech
quests.directSpeech: The CEO said, "Our profits grew by 12% last quarter. Can the team confirm the final figures by Friday? Please send them to me here as soon as they're ready."
quests.reportedSpeech: The CEO said that their profits had grown by 12% the previous quarter, asked whether the team could confirm the final figures by Friday, and asked to have them sent there as soon as they were ready.
changesList: question word order → statement word order
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Grew' becomes 'had grown', 'last quarter' becomes 'the previous quarter', 'can confirm' becomes 'could confirm' with statement word order, and 'here' becomes 'there'.
quests.nativeTip: This passage has three functions — a statement, a question, and a request — combine the correct backshift, pronoun, time word, and word order for each.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The CEO said, "Our profits grew by 12% last quarter. Can the team confirm the final figures by Friday? Please send them to me here as soon as they're ready."" ➔ "The CEO said that their profits had grown by 12% the previous quarter, asked whether the team could confirm the final figures by Friday, and asked to have them sent there as soon as they were ready."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Indirect-to-Direct Reconstruction

quests.reportedSpeech: The nurse said, "You have to stay in bed. Has the pain improved since yesterday?"
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Had to' reverses to 'have to', 'had improved' reverses to 'has improved', and 'the previous day' reverses to 'yesterday'.
quests.nativeTip: Reverse both the obligation phrase and the question, along with the time expression.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The nurse told the patient that she had to stay in bed and asked whether the pain had improved since the previous day." ➔ "The nurse said, "You have to stay in bed. Has the pain improved since yesterday?""

quests.directSpeech: Camila said, "I know this seems sudden, but I've decided to accept the job offer, and I start next month."
quests.reportedSpeech: Camila said that she knew that seemed sudden but that she had decided to accept the job offer and that she started the following month.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'This' becomes 'that', 'know' becomes 'knew', 'seems' becomes 'seemed', 've decided' becomes 'had decided', 'start' becomes 'started', and 'next month' becomes 'the following month'.
quests.nativeTip: Track the demonstrative, the present-perfect backshift, and the time word across three connected clauses.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Camila said, "I know this seems sudden, but I've decided to accept the job offer, and I start next month."" ➔ "Camila said that she knew that seemed sudden but that she had decided to accept the job offer and that she started the following month."

quests.ruleExplanation: 'Must' becomes 'had to', 'can' becomes 'could', 'this' becomes 'that', and 'next month' becomes 'the following month'.
quests.nativeTip: Two different modals appear here — check that both genuinely backshift, unlike the exceptions you studied earlier.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The technician said, "This part must be replaced immediately, though the other one can probably wait until next month."" ➔ "The technician said that that part had to be replaced immediately, though the other one could probably wait until the following month."

quests.reportedSpeech: The professor said that gravity causes objects to fall at the same rate regardless of mass, which was why she always used that experiment to teach the concept.
quests.ruleExplanation: The scientific fact 'causes' stays unchanged, but 'is why' becomes 'was why', 'use' becomes 'used', and 'this' becomes 'that', since those describe the professor's own teaching habit, not a universal truth.
quests.nativeTip: Only one clause here is a scientific fact — compare it carefully with the personal habit clause that does backshift.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The professor said, "Gravity causes objects to fall at the same rate regardless of mass, which is why I always use this experiment to teach the concept."" ➔ "The professor said that gravity causes objects to fall at the same rate regardless of mass, which was why she always used that experiment to teach the concept."

quests.ruleExplanation: 'Might' and 'should' both remain unchanged since they are already past-compatible forms; 'you'/'tonight'/'this weekend' shift to 'me'/'that night'/'that weekend', and 'want' becomes 'wanted'.
quests.nativeTip: Two modals appear here that should stay unchanged — 'might' and 'should' — check that they aren't mistakenly backshifted further.

quests.directSpeech: The graduating class president said, "We've faced challenges that none of us expected, but because we supported each other, we're leaving here stronger than when we arrived, and I know that whatever comes next, we'll handle it the way we've handled everything this year — together."
quests.reportedSpeech: The graduating class president said that they had faced challenges that none of them had expected, but that because they had supported each other, they were leaving there stronger than when they had arrived, and that she knew that whatever came next, they would handle it the way they had handled everything that year — together.
quests.ruleExplanation: Every verb backshifts consistently ('ve faced'/'expected' become 'had faced'/'had expected', 'supported' becomes 'had supported', 'are leaving' becomes 'were leaving', 'arrived' becomes 'had arrived', 'know'/'comes'/'will handle'/'ve handled' become 'knew'/'came'/'would handle'/'had handled'), 'here' becomes 'there', and 'this year' becomes 'that year'.
quests.nativeTip: This final capstone question combines nearly every rule from the whole course — pronouns, tense backshift at multiple levels, the place word, the time word, and a whatever-clause with its own backshift — all within one flowing sentence.
